name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on new rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing still in force
state: China's commerce ministry announced on 9 Nov that its suspension of export controls on some critical minerals, due to end on 10 Nov, is extended for two months to 10 Jan 2027 alongside the wider US–China trade truce (The National). The extension is short, and the April 2025 licensing requirements for seven rare earths remain in force, so Watch holds. No production stoppages outside China were found.
for_you: Supply of magnets and rare earths used in cars, electronics and defence remains subject to Chinese licensing, with the next deadline on 10 Jan 2027. Manufacturers reliant on Chinese inputs are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Licensing controls still slowing exports; Oct 2025 controls paused only to 10 Jan 2027; no stoppages outside China

sources.title: The National — China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
